title: Groundwater's most-used public records
summary: Well Completion Reports and Periodic Groundwater Level Measurements are among the most-viewed water datasets on either portal, about 19,000 and 15,600 page views. Local agencies implementing SGMA, consultants and researchers lean on them to see where wells are and how water levels move.
ab1755_angle: §12415(b) names groundwater levels. These are DWR program data published on CNRA and federated to data.ca.gov, the model the 2018 plan intended.

title: Mapping every field in the state
summary: DWR's Statewide Crop Mapping is the single most-viewed water dataset across both portals, with about 20,900 page views. Field-level land-use maps feed agricultural water-use estimates, groundwater budgets and SGMA plans.
ab1755_angle: Land use is one of the DWR data types §12415(b) requires on the platform.

title: Watching the ground sink, from space and the air
summary: Satellite InSAR subsidence data (about 10,900 views) and DWR's airborne electromagnetic (AEM) surveys (about 8,300 views) give an open, statewide picture of land subsidence and aquifer structure. Before these, that picture lived in scattered studies.
ab1755_angle: These are new collection programs whose data was open from the start, an example of plan action 1.2.4 (support new data collection to fill gaps).
datasets: TRE ALTAMIRA InSAR Subsidence Data|https://data.cnra.ca.gov/dataset/tre-altamira-insar-subsidence ; DWR Airborne Electromagnetic (AEM) Surveys Data|https://data.cnra.ca.gov/dataset/aem

title: Is it safe to swim?
summary: The State Water Board's freshwater harmful algal bloom and fecal indicator bacteria datasets are the two most-viewed Water Board datasets, about 10,300 and 9,800 views. They are updated frequently and sit behind bloom maps and swim-safety tools.
ab1755_angle: Water quality is a §12415(b) data type. Most of the views land on data.ca.gov, where the Water Board publishes, not on the CNRA copy.
datasets: Surface Water - Freshwater Harmful Algal Blooms|https://data.ca.gov/dataset/surface-water-freshwater-harmful-algal-blooms ; Surface Water - Fecal Indicator Bacteria Monitoring Results|https://data.ca.gov/dataset/surface-water-fecal-indicator-bacteria-results

title: Wastewater as an early-warning system
summary: During the pandemic, wastewater testing for SARS-CoV-2 became a leading indicator of community spread. The State Water Board's open dataset has drawn about 9,500 views across both portals.
ab1755_angle: Not a use case anyone wrote in 2018. It shows the plan's point that open-by-default data finds uses its publishers did not anticipate.

title: Water rights data comes into the open
summary: Reported water use and water-right seasons became open datasets in 2021. In October 2025 the Water Board introduced CalWATRS to replace eWRIMS, making the state's roughly 40,000 water-rights records easily accessible to the public.
ab1755_angle: §12415(b) names water rights and diversions. They arrived through the Water Board's own modernization program (UPWARD/CalWATRS), not through AB 1755 itself.
datasets: California Water Rights Water Use Reported|https://data.ca.gov/dataset/california-water-rights-water-use-reported ; California Water Rights Uses and Seasons|https://data.ca.gov/dataset/california-water-rights-uses-and-seasons

title: Which small systems run dry first?
summary: DWR's Drought and Water Shortage Risk dataset scores small suppliers and rural communities. It has about 3,000 views and was built to help the state plan drought assistance. Newer urban water data packages carry the drought picture forward.
ab1755_angle: Data built for a specific decision, the use-case approach of plan objective 1.1.
datasets: Drought and Water Shortage Risk: Small Suppliers and Rural Communities|https://data.cnra.ca.gov/dataset/drought-risk-small-suppliers-and-communities ; Urban Water Data - Drought Planning and Management|https://data.cnra.ca.gov/dataset/urban-water-data-drought

title: An open-source groundwater accounting platform
summary: DWR, the State Water Board, the California Water Data Consortium and Environmental Defense Fund partnered on an open-source platform and data standards. Groundwater agencies can use it to track water budgets and allocations.
ab1755_angle: The Consortium's flagship pilot, and the clearest example of the §12410(b) nonprofit partnership doing what the 2018 plan's pilot actions (4.1) described.

title: Civic technologists take on drinking water
summary: The 2018 Safe Drinking Water Data Challenge (OPR and the West Big Data Hub) invited teams to build tools from open drinking water data, followed by a 2019 Water Data Challenge. The Water Board's 2023 Open Environmental Data Project workshop continued the thread.
ab1755_angle: Plan action 4.4.3 (data challenges and hackathons), one of the few strategic actions scored Done.
datasets: Drinking Water - Open Environmental Data Project (2023 workshop)|https://data.ca.gov/dataset/drinking-water-open-environmental-data-project-march-23-2023-workshop

title: The missing water market
summary: §12415(c) requires data on completed water transfers: volume, price, buyers, sellers and the water right. Ten years on, the portals hold one transfers dataset, covering State Water Project-facilitated non-project transfers, with about 1,000 views.
ab1755_angle: A story of absence: the statute's most specific market-transparency requirement remains largely unmet.
datasets: State Water Project Facilitated Non-Project Water Transfers|https://data.cnra.ca.gov/dataset/state-water-project-facilitated-non-project-water-transfers
